summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: most Hindi videos get 1,000-1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly get under 60 views. The best performers are short 'X doesn't do what you think, it only does Y' explainers on relatable robots and sensors (gyro robot, clap switch, IR robot, DHT11). Generic 'How does X work?' titles on everyday items (taps, lift, mall door, smoke alarm) and the one English video do poorly, and some videos have no Instagram numbers at all.
winningPattern: Hindi, Instagram-first Reels about a hands-on maker subject (robots, clap switch, DHT11, mic) with a myth-busting contrast hook like 'X doesn't see/hear Y, it only senses Z' or 'Without X this robot falls instantly'. Titles are short and punchy with one emoji, and a surprising concrete claim rather than a plain question. Robot and Arduino-module topics get the most saves and shares; the contrast hook gets the most likes.
doMore: Use the 'doesn't do A, only does B' contrast hook in the first line of every video
Make more robot and Arduino-module videos (gyro, IR, line follower, clap switch), since they get the most saves and shares
Post every video on Instagram Reels first, then repost to YouTube with a stronger first 2 seconds
End with a clear save/share prompt, like 'Save this for your next project', since saves and shares signal value
Make follow-ups of winners, like a clap switch part 3 or a gyro robot demo, as the clap switch series did well
stopDoing: Plain 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' question titles on everyday items like taps, lifts and doors
Posting videos on only one platform, since several have zero Instagram data
Publishing near-duplicate topics (smoke alarm, IR sensor, tap) with little new angle
